/*
 * ESP32-S3-LCD-2 SD Card Diagnostic Tool
 * Tests multiple SPI modes and provides detailed debugging
 */

#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"
#include "driver/sdspi_host.h"
#include "sdmmc_cmd.h"

// Pin definitions from schematic
#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

// Test different SPI frequencies (Hz)
const uint32_t spiFrequencies[] = {
  400000,    // 400 KHz - SD init speed
  1000000,   // 1 MHz
  4000000,   // 4 MHz
  8000000,   // 8 MHz
  10000000,  // 10 MHz
  16000000,  // 16 MHz
  20000000   // 20 MHz
};

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  while (!Serial) {
    delay(10);
  }
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n\n=== ESP32-S3-LCD-2 SD Card Diagnostics ===");
  Serial.println("Hardware: Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-2");
  Serial.println("SD Pins: CS=41, MOSI=38, MISO=40, SCK=39\n");

  // Test 1: GPIO availability check
  Serial.println("TEST 1: GPIO Availability Check");
  testGPIOAvailability();
  delay(1000);

  // Test 2: SPI bus initialization
  Serial.println("\nTEST 2: SPI Bus Initialization");
  testSPIInit();
  delay(1000);

  // Test 3: SD card detection with different speeds
  Serial.println("\nTEST 3: SD Card Detection (Multiple Speeds)");
  testSDCardSpeeds();
  delay(1000);

  // Test 4: SDMMC mode (if supported)
  Serial.println("\nTEST 4: SDMMC Mode Test");
  testSDMMCMode();
  delay(1000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Diagnostic Complete ===");
  Serial.println("If all tests failed, check:");
  Serial.println("1. SD card is formatted as FAT32");
  Serial.println("2. SD card is properly inserted");
  Serial.println("3. SD card is not write-protected");
  Serial.println("4. Try a different SD card (some cards are incompatible)");
  Serial.println("5. Check for hardware conflicts with LCD/Camera");
}

void loop() {
  delay(1000);
}

void testGPIOAvailability() {
  Serial.println("Checking if GPIO pins can be configured...");

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  Serial.printf("  CS   (GPIO %d): %s\n", SD_CS, digitalRead(SD_CS) == HIGH ? "OK" : "FAIL");

  pinMode(SD_MOSI, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_MOSI, HIGH);
  Serial.printf("  MOSI (GPIO %d): %s\n", SD_MOSI, digitalRead(SD_MOSI) == HIGH ? "OK" : "FAIL");

  pinMode(SD_MISO, INPUT_PULLUP);
  Serial.printf("  MISO (GPIO %d): %s (pullup: %d)\n", SD_MISO, "OK", digitalRead(SD_MISO));

  pinMode(SD_SCK, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_SCK, LOW);
  Serial.printf("  SCK  (GPIO %d): %s\n", SD_SCK, digitalRead(SD_SCK) == LOW ? "OK" : "FAIL");

  Serial.println("GPIO configuration: PASSED");
}

void testSPIInit() {
  Serial.println("Initializing SPI bus...");

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  Serial.println("  SPI.begin(): SUCCESS");

  // Test SPI transfer
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  uint8_t response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  Serial.printf("  SPI test transfer: 0x%02X\n", response);

  SPI.end();
}

void testSDCardSpeeds() {
  for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(spiFrequencies) / sizeof(spiFrequencies[0]); i++) {
    uint32_t freq = spiFrequencies[i];
    Serial.printf("\n--- Testing at %lu Hz (%.1f MHz) ---\n", freq, freq / 1000000.0);

    SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
    SPI.setFrequency(freq);

    if (SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI, freq)) {
      Serial.println("✓ SD CARD DETECTED!");

      uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();
      Serial.print("  Card Type: ");
      switch (cardType) {
        case CARD_NONE: Serial.println("NONE"); break;
        case CARD_MMC:  Serial.println("MMC"); break;
        case CARD_SD:   Serial.println("SDSC"); break;
        case CARD_SDHC: Serial.println("SDHC"); break;
        default:        Serial.println("UNKNOWN"); break;
      }

      if (cardType != CARD_NONE) {
        uint64_t cardSize = SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024);
        Serial.printf("  Card Size: %llu MB\n", cardSize);
        Serial.printf("  Total Space: %llu MB\n", SD.totalBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
        Serial.printf("  Used Space: %llu MB\n", SD.usedBytes() / (1024 * 1024));

        // Try to list root directory
        Serial.println("  Root directory contents:");
        listDir(SD, "/", 0);

        SD.end();
        SPI.end();

        Serial.println("\n✓✓✓ SUCCESS! SD card working at this frequency ✓✓✓");
        return;
      }

      SD.end();
    } else {
      Serial.println("✗ SD.begin() FAILED");
    }

    SPI.end();
    delay(500);
  }

  Serial.println("\n✗✗✗ FAILED at all frequencies ✗✗✗");
}

void testSDMMCMode() {
  Serial.println("Testing SDMMC 1-bit mode (alternative to SPI)...");
  Serial.println("Note: This may not work if LCD shares these pins");

  // SDMMC 1-bit mode uses: CMD, CLK, D0
  // We'll try mapping to our SPI pins

  Serial.println("  Skipped - use SPI mode for this board");
}

void listDir(fs::FS &fs, const char *dirname, uint8_t levels) {
  File root = fs.open(dirname);
  if (!root) {
    Serial.println("    Failed to open directory");
    return;
  }
  if (!root.isDirectory()) {
    Serial.println("    Not a directory");
    return;
  }

  File file = root.openNextFile();
  int count = 0;
  while (file && count < 10) {
    if (file.isDirectory()) {
      Serial.printf("    DIR : %s\n", file.name());
    } else {
      Serial.printf("    FILE: %-20s  SIZE: %d bytes\n", file.name(), file.size());
    }
    file = root.openNextFile();
    count++;
  }

  if (count == 0) {
    Serial.println("    (empty)");
  }
}

/*
 * ESP32-S3 SD Card Bus Scanner
 * Scans all available SPI buses and GPIO combinations
 */

#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"

// Known pin configuration from schematic
#define SD_CS_KNOWN   41
#define SD_MOSI_KNOWN 38
#define SD_MISO_KNOWN 40
#define SD_SCK_KNOWN  39

// Alternative SPI bus configurations to test
struct SPIConfig {
  int8_t sck;
  int8_t miso;
  int8_t mosi;
  int8_t cs;
  const char* name;
};

// Test configurations
SPIConfig configs[] = {
  {39, 40, 38, 41, "Schematic (Default)"},
  {39, 40, 38, 45, "CS=45 (LCD_CS)"},
  {14, 13, 11, 10, "ESP32-S3 SPI defaults"},
  {12, 13, 11, 10, "Alt ESP32-S3 SPI"},
  {18, 19, 23,  5, "ESP32 legacy SPI"},
  {36, 37, 35, 34, "High GPIO SPI"}
};

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  while (!Serial) {
    delay(10);
  }
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== ESP32-S3 SD Card Bus Scanner ===\n");
  Serial.println("This will test multiple SPI bus configurations");
  Serial.println("to find any working SD card connection.\n");

  // Test each configuration
  for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(configs) / sizeof(configs[0]); i++) {
    testConfig(configs[i]);
    delay(1000);
  }

  Serial.println("\n=== Scan Complete ===");
}

void loop() {
  delay(1000);
}

void testConfig(SPIConfig cfg) {
  Serial.println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━");
  Serial.printf("Testing: %s\n", cfg.name);
  Serial.printf("  SCK=%d, MISO=%d, MOSI=%d, CS=%d\n", cfg.sck, cfg.miso, cfg.mosi, cfg.cs);

  // Initialize SPI with this configuration
  SPI.begin(cfg.sck, cfg.miso, cfg.mosi, cfg.cs);

  // Try different frequencies
  uint32_t frequencies[] = {400000, 1000000, 4000000, 10000000};

  for (int f = 0; f < 4; f++) {
    uint32_t freq = frequencies[f];
    Serial.printf("\n  @ %.1f MHz: ", freq / 1000000.0);

    if (SD.begin(cfg.cs, SPI, freq)) {
      uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();

      if (cardType != CARD_NONE) {
        Serial.println("✓✓✓ CARD FOUND! ✓✓✓");
        Serial.printf("    Type: ");
        switch (cardType) {
          case CARD_MMC:  Serial.println("MMC"); break;
          case CARD_SD:   Serial.println("SDSC"); break;
          case CARD_SDHC: Serial.println("SDHC"); break;
          default:        Serial.println("UNKNOWN"); break;
        }
        Serial.printf("    Size: %llu MB\n", SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024));

        // Quick read/write test
        if (quickReadWriteTest()) {
          Serial.println("    Read/Write: ✓ WORKING");
          Serial.println("\n╔════════════════════════════════════╗");
          Serial.println("║  ✓ SUCCESS! USE THIS CONFIG! ✓    ║");
          Serial.println("╚════════════════════════════════════╝");
        } else {
          Serial.println("    Read/Write: ✗ FAILED");
        }

        SD.end();
        SPI.end();
        return;
      }
    }
    Serial.println("✗ Not found");
    SD.end();
  }

  SPI.end();
  Serial.println("Result: No card detected\n");
}

bool quickReadWriteTest() {
  const char* testFile = "/test_scan.txt";
  const char* testData = "SD_SCAN_TEST";

  // Write test
  File file = SD.open(testFile, FILE_WRITE);
  if (!file) return false;

  size_t written = file.print(testData);
  file.close();
  if (written != strlen(testData)) return false;

  // Read test
  file = SD.open(testFile);
  if (!file) return false;

  char buffer[32] = {0};
  file.readBytes(buffer, strlen(testData));
  file.close();

  // Cleanup
  SD.remove(testFile);

  return strcmp(buffer, testData) == 0;
}

/*
 * Minimal SD Card Test - ESP32-S3-LCD-2
 * Bare minimum code to test SD card
 */

#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(3000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Minimal SD Test ===");
  Serial.println("Pins: CS=41, MOSI=38, MISO=40, SCK=39\n");

  // Method 1: Simple SD.begin()
  Serial.println("Method 1: Simple SD.begin()");
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  if (SD.begin(SD_CS)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD CARD MOUNTED!");
    printCardInfo();
    SD.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ SD.begin() failed");
  }
  SPI.end();
  delay(1000);

  // Method 2: Explicit SPI object
  Serial.println("\nMethod 2: With explicit SPI");
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD CARD MOUNTED!");
    printCardInfo();
    SD.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ SD.begin(CS, SPI) failed");
  }
  SPI.end();
  delay(1000);

  // Method 3: Low frequency (400kHz - SD initialization speed)
  Serial.println("\nMethod 3: Low frequency (400 kHz)");
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI, 400000)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD CARD MOUNTED!");
    printCardInfo();
    SD.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ SD.begin() @ 400kHz failed");
  }
  SPI.end();
  delay(1000);

  // Method 4: Very low frequency (100kHz)
  Serial.println("\nMethod 4: Very low frequency (100 kHz)");
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI, 100000)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD CARD MOUNTED!");
    printCardInfo();
    SD.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ SD.begin() @ 100kHz failed");
  }
  SPI.end();

  Serial.println("\n=== Test Complete ===");
  Serial.println("\nIf all methods failed:");
  Serial.println("1. Verify SD card is FAT32 formatted");
  Serial.println("2. Try a different SD card (2GB-32GB recommended)");
  Serial.println("3. Check card is fully inserted");
  Serial.println("4. Run the bus scanner sketch");
}

void loop() {
  delay(1000);
}

void printCardInfo() {
  uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();
  Serial.print("  Card Type: ");
  switch (cardType) {
    case CARD_MMC:  Serial.println("MMC"); break;
    case CARD_SD:   Serial.println("SDSC"); break;
    case CARD_SDHC: Serial.println("SDHC/SDXC"); break;
    default:        Serial.println("UNKNOWN"); break;
  }

  uint64_t cardSize = SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024);
  Serial.printf("  Size: %llu MB\n", cardSize);
  Serial.printf("  Total: %llu MB\n", SD.totalBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
  Serial.printf("  Used: %llu MB\n", SD.usedBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
}

I've created three diagnostic sketches in [workbench/](workbench/) to help troubleshoot your SD card issue:

## 1. **sd_minimal_test** - Start here!
The simplest test with 4 different initialization methods and frequencies (100kHz to default). This will quickly tell you if the SD card can be detected at all.

## 2. **sd_card_diagnostics** - Comprehensive testing
Tests:
- GPIO pin availability
- SPI bus initialization
- Multiple SPI frequencies (400kHz to 20MHz)
- Detailed card information
- Directory listing

## 3. **sd_card_bus_scanner** - Alternative pin finder
Scans 6 different SPI bus configurations including:
- Your schematic pins (39/40/38/41)
- Alternative CS pins (LCD might be interfering)
- Standard ESP32-S3 SPI defaults
- Performs read/write tests on detected cards

## How to Use:

1. **Start with sd_minimal_test** - Upload and check serial monitor
2. If that fails, run **sd_card_diagnostics** for detailed info
3. If still failing, run **sd_card_bus_scanner** to check for pin conflicts

## Common Issues to Check:

Based on the schematic, **the SPI bus is shared between SD card and LCD** (pins 38, 39, 40). This could cause conflicts!

- Make sure no LCD initialization code runs before SD card access
- Try different CS pin if LCD is holding the bus
- Verify your SD card is FAT32 formatted (not exFAT)
- Use a quality SD card (2GB-32GB works best)
- Check card is fully inserted and not write-protected

Upload the minimal test first and share the serial output - that will tell us exactly what's happening!

/*
 * Raw SPI SD Card Detection Test
 * Sends CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE) directly to check if card responds
 */

#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Raw SD Card SPI Test ===");

  // Test 1: Check MISO pin state (card should pull it high when idle)
  pinMode(SD_MISO, INPUT_PULLUP);
  delay(100);
  int misoState = digitalRead(SD_MISO);
  Serial.printf("MISO idle state: %s (should be HIGH if card present)\n",
                misoState ? "HIGH" : "LOW");

  // Test 2: Initialize SPI and try raw CMD0
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000); // SD init frequency

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  delay(10);

  // Send dummy clocks with CS high
  Serial.println("\nSending init clocks...");
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // Send CMD0: GO_IDLE_STATE
  Serial.println("Sending CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE)...");
  uint8_t response = sendCmd(0, 0);
  Serial.printf("Response: 0x%02X ", response);

  if (response == 0x01) {
    Serial.println("✓ CARD RESPONDED! Card is in IDLE state");

    // Try CMD8 (voltage check)
    Serial.println("\nSending CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND)...");
    uint8_t r7[5];
    r7[0] = sendCmd(8, 0x1AA);
    for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
      r7[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    }
    Serial.printf("Response: 0x%02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
                  r7[0], r7[1], r7[2], r7[3], r7[4]);

    if (r7[0] == 0x01) {
      Serial.println("✓ SD Card v2.0+ detected");
    }

  } else if (response == 0xFF) {
    Serial.println("✗ No response (0xFF) - Card not present or not responding");
  } else {
    Serial.printf("✗ Unexpected response (expected 0x01 for idle)\n");
  }

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.end();

  // Test 3: Check for card detect pin
  Serial.println("\n=== Hardware Detection ===");
  Serial.println("Checking common card-detect pins:");

  int cdPins[] = {42, 43, 44, 46};  // Common CD pins
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    pinMode(cdPins[i], INPUT_PULLUP);
    delay(10);
    Serial.printf("  GPIO%d: %s\n", cdPins[i], digitalRead(cdPins[i]) ? "HIGH" : "LOW");
  }

  Serial.println("\n=== Summary ===");
  Serial.println("If CMD0 response was 0xFF:");
  Serial.println("  • Card slot may be empty");
  Serial.println("  • Card not making contact");
  Serial.println("  • Wrong pins (but schematic shows 41/38/40/39)");
  Serial.println("  • Hardware fault on SD slot");
}

void loop() {}

uint8_t sendCmd(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delay(1);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);           // Command byte
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);   // Argument bits 31-24
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);   // Argument bits 23-16
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);    // Argument bits 15-8
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);           // Argument bits 7-0

  uint8_t crc = 0x01; // Default CRC
  if (cmd == 0) crc = 0x95;  // Valid CRC for CMD0
  if (cmd == 8) crc = 0x87;  // Valid CRC for CMD8
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  // Wait for response (max 8 bytes)
  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (response != 0xFF) break;
  }

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF); // Extra clock

  return response;
}

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(SD_MOSI, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(SD_SCK, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(SD_MISO, INPUT_PULLUP);

  Serial.println("\nToggling CS (GPIO41) 10 times...");
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    delay(100);
    Serial.printf("  CS HIGH\n");
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
    delay(100);
    Serial.printf("  CS LOW\n");
  }
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  Serial.println("\nToggling SCK (GPIO39) 10 times...");
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    digitalWrite(SD_SCK, HIGH);
    delayMicroseconds(500);
    digitalWrite(SD_SCK, LOW);
    delayMicroseconds(500);
  }
  Serial.println("  Done");

  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {

    delay(50);
    digitalWrite(SD_MOSI, LOW);
    delay(50);
  }
  Serial.println("  Done");

  Serial.println("\nReading MISO (GPIO40) 20 times...");
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    int state = digitalRead(SD_MISO);
    Serial.printf("  MISO: %s\n", state ? "HIGH" : "LOW");
    delay(100);
  }

  // Check for floating or stuck pins
  Serial.println("\n=== Pin State Analysis ===");

  pinMode(SD_CS, INPUT);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("CS (no pullup): %s\n", digitalRead(SD_CS) ? "HIGH/Float" : "LOW/GND");
  pinMode(SD_CS, INPUT_PULLUP);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("CS (pullup):    %s\n", digitalRead(SD_CS) ? "HIGH" : "LOW/Stuck");

  pinMode(SD_MOSI, INPUT);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("MOSI (no pullup): %s\n", digitalRead(SD_MOSI) ? "HIGH/Float" : "LOW/GND");
  pinMode(SD_MOSI, INPUT_PULLUP);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("MOSI (pullup):    %s\n", digitalRead(SD_MOSI) ? "HIGH" : "LOW/Stuck");

  pinMode(SD_SCK, INPUT);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("SCK (no pullup): %s\n", digitalRead(SD_SCK) ? "HIGH/Float" : "LOW/GND");
  pinMode(SD_SCK, INPUT_PULLUP);
  delay(10);
  Serial.printf("SCK (pullup):    %s\n", digitalRead(SD_SCK) ? "HIGH" : "LOW/Stuck");

  pinMode(SD_MISO, INPUT);

/*
 * Factory SD Card Test - Based on Waveshare factory demo
 * Mimics exact initialization from working factory firmware
 */

#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Factory-Style SD Test ===");

  // Method from factory demo (03_sd_card_test)
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI);

  Serial.println("Attempting SD.begin(41)...");
  if (!SD.begin(SD_CS)) {
    Serial.println("✗ FAILED - Card Mount Failed");
    testAlternatives();
    return;
  }

  Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS - Card Mounted!");

  uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();
  if (cardType == CARD_NONE) {
    Serial.println("✗ No SD card attached");
    SD.end();
    return;
  }

  Serial.print("Card Type: ");
  if (cardType == CARD_MMC) Serial.println("MMC");
  else if (cardType == CARD_SD) Serial.println("SDSC");
  else if (cardType == CARD_SDHC) Serial.println("SDHC");
  else Serial.println("UNKNOWN");

  uint64_t cardSize = SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024);
  Serial.printf("Size: %lluMB\n", cardSize);
  Serial.printf("Total: %lluMB\n", SD.totalBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
  Serial.printf("Used: %lluMB\n", SD.usedBytes() / (1024 * 1024));

  // Try basic operations
  listDir(SD, "/", 0);

  File file = SD.open("/test_factory.txt", FILE_WRITE);
  if (file) {
    file.println("Factory test OK");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("Write test: OK");
  } else {
    Serial.println("Write test: FAILED");
  }

  SD.end();
}

void loop() {}

void testAlternatives() {
  Serial.println("\nTrying alternative methods...");

  // Alt 1: Reinit SPI with CS
  Serial.println("\n[1] SPI.begin with CS parameter");
  SPI.end();
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS)) {
    Serial.println("✓ This worked!");
    printInfo();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  // Alt 2: Manual CS control
  Serial.println("\n[2] Manual CS control");
  SPI.end();
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  delay(100);
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI);
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS)) {
    Serial.println("✓ This worked!");
    printInfo();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  // Alt 3: VSPI (ESP32-S3 has SPI2/SPI3)
  Serial.println("\n[3] Using VSPI instance");
  SPIClass vspi(VSPI);
  vspi.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, vspi)) {
    Serial.println("✓ This worked!");
    printInfo();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\n=== All methods exhausted ===");
}

void printInfo() {
  Serial.printf("  Type: %d\n", SD.cardType());
  Serial.printf("  Size: %lluMB\n", SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024));
}

void listDir(fs::FS &fs, const char *dirname, uint8_t levels) {
  Serial.printf("Listing: %s\n", dirname);

  File root = fs.open(dirname);
  if (!root || !root.isDirectory()) {
    Serial.println("  Not a directory");
    return;
  }

  File file = root.openNextFile();
  int count = 0;
  while (file && count < 5) {
    if (file.isDirectory()) {
      Serial.printf("  DIR: %s\n", file.name());
    } else {
      Serial.printf("  %s (%d bytes)\n", file.name(), file.size());
    }
    file = root.openNextFile();
    count++;
  }
  if (count == 0) Serial.println("  (empty)");
}

## Likely Issues:

Given that **all tests fail at all frequencies with 0xFF responses**, this points to:

1. **SD card not inserted properly** - Most likely! Check the slot carefully
2. **SD card slot damaged/not making contact** - Inspect the spring contacts
3. **Wrong SD card format** - Must be FAT32, not exFAT
4. **Defective/incompatible SD card** - Try a different card (older 2-8GB cards work best)
5. **Board defect** - SD traces not connected (less likely on new board)

Try **sd_raw_spi_test** - if it shows `0xFF` for CMD0, the card is definitely not responding at the hardware level. That means it's a physical issue, not software.

/*
 * Manual SD Card Initialization
 * Since raw commands work, bypass library init issues
 */

#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"
#include "sd_defines.h"
#include "sd_diskio.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

SPIClass *spi = NULL;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Manual SD Init ===");

  // Pre-init: Set CS high before SPI starts
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  delay(100);

  // Init SPI at slow speed
  spi = new SPIClass(HSPI);
  spi->begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  Serial.println("Method 1: Very slow init (250kHz)");
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, *spi, 250000, "/sd", 5)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS!");
    printCardInfo();
    testReadWrite();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\nMethod 2: Max open files = 1");
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, *spi, 400000, "/sd", 1)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS!");
    printCardInfo();
    testReadWrite();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\nMethod 3: Different mount point");
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, *spi, 400000, "/sdcard", 5)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS!");
    printCardInfo();
    testReadWrite();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\nMethod 4: Format on fail");
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, *spi, 400000, "/sd", 5, true)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS!");
    printCardInfo();
    testReadWrite();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\nMethod 5: Simple with HSPI");
  if (SD.begin(SD_CS, *spi)) {
    Serial.println("✓ SUCCESS!");
    printCardInfo();
    testReadWrite();
    SD.end();
    return;
  }
  Serial.println("✗ Failed");

  Serial.println("\nAll methods failed");
}

void loop() {}

}

/*
 * Deep SD Debug - Manual card initialization
 * Step-by-step SD protocol to find where it breaks
 */

#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

uint8_t cardType = 0;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Deep SD Protocol Debug ===");

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  delay(10);

  // Step 1: Send 80+ clocks with CS high
  Serial.println("\nStep 1: Power-on init (80 clocks)");
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }
  Serial.println("  Done");

  // Step 2: CMD0 - Reset card
  Serial.println("\nStep 2: CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE)");
  uint8_t r1 = sendCommand(0, 0, 0x95);
  Serial.printf("  R1: 0x%02X %s\n", r1, (r1 == 0x01) ? "✓" : "✗");
  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.println("  FAILED - Card not entering idle");
    return;
  }

  // Step 3: CMD8 - Check voltage
  Serial.println("\nStep 3: CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND)");
  uint8_t r7[5];
  r7[0] = sendCommand(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
    r7[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }
  Serial.printf("  R7: 0x%02X %02X %02X %02X %02X ", r7[0], r7[1], r7[2], r7[3], r7[4]);

  if (r7[0] == 0x01 && r7[3] == 0x01 && r7[4] == 0xAA) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD v2.0");
    cardType = 2;
  } else if (r7[0] == 0x05) {
    Serial.println("✓ SD v1.x");
    cardType = 1;
  } else {
    Serial.printf("? Unexpected (continuing anyway)\n");
    cardType = 1;
  }

  // Step 4: CMD55 + ACMD41 - Initialize card
  Serial.println("\nStep 4: ACMD41 (INIT) loop");
  int attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 100) {
    // CMD55 first
    r1 = sendCommand(55, 0, 0xFF);
    if (r1 > 1) {
      Serial.printf("  CMD55 failed: 0x%02X\n", r1);
      break;
    }

    // ACMD41 with HCS bit for SDHC
    uint32_t arg = (cardType == 2) ? 0x40000000 : 0x00000000;
    r1 = sendCommand(41, arg, 0xFF);

    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("  ✓ Ready after %d attempts\n", attempts + 1);
      break;
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(10);
  }

  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    Serial.printf("  ✗ FAILED after %d attempts (R1=0x%02X)\n", attempts, r1);
    Serial.println("\n*** ACMD41 INITIALIZATION FAILED ***");
    Serial.println("This is where the library fails!");
    return;
  }

  // Step 5: CMD58 - Read OCR
  Serial.println("\nStep 5: CMD58 (READ_OCR)");
  uint8_t ocr[5];
  ocr[0] = sendCommand(58, 0, 0xFF);
  for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
    ocr[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }
  Serial.printf("  OCR: 0x%02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
                ocr[0], ocr[1], ocr[2], ocr[3], ocr[4]);

  if (ocr[0] == 0x00 && (ocr[1] & 0x40)) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ SDHC/SDXC card");
  } else if (ocr[0] == 0x00) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ SDSC card");
  }

  // Step 6: Switch to faster speed
  Serial.println("\nStep 6: Switch to 10MHz");
  SPI.setFrequency(10000000);
  Serial.println("  Done");

  // Step 7: CMD16 - Set block size (if SDSC)
  if (!(ocr[1] & 0x40)) {
    Serial.println("\nStep 7: CMD16 (SET_BLOCKLEN)");
    r1 = sendCommand(16, 512, 0xFF);
    Serial.printf("  R1: 0x%02X %s\n", r1, (r1 == 0x00) ? "✓" : "✗");
  }

  // Step 8: Try to read sector 0
  Serial.println("\nStep 8: CMD17 (READ_SINGLE_BLOCK) sector 0");
  r1 = sendCommand(17, 0, 0xFF);
  Serial.printf("  R1: 0x%02X %s\n", r1, (r1 == 0x00) ? "✓" : "✗");

  if (r1 == 0x00) {
    // Wait for data token
    uint8_t token;
    int timeout = 1000;
    while (timeout-- > 0) {
      token = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
      if (token == 0xFE) break;
      delayMicroseconds(100);
    }

    if (token == 0xFE) {
      Serial.println("  ✓ Data token received");

      // Read first 32 bytes
      Serial.print("  Data: ");
      for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
        uint8_t b = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
        Serial.printf("%02X ", b);
      }

      // Skip rest + CRC
      for (int i = 32; i < 514; i++) {
        SPI.transfer(0xFF);
      }

      Serial.println("\n  ✓✓ RAW SECTOR READ WORKS!");
      Serial.println("\n*** Card is fully functional at protocol level! ***");
    } else {
      Serial.printf("  ✗ No data token (got 0x%02X)\n", token);
    }
  }

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  Serial.println("\n=== Analysis ===");
  Serial.println("If ACMD41 failed: Card won't initialize");
  Serial.println("If sector read worked: Card is OK, library has bug");
}

void loop() {}

uint8_t sendCommand(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(10);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  // Wait for response
  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
  }

  return response;
}

Created two critical debug sketches:

## **sd_deep_debug** ⭐ Run this!
Goes through the entire SD initialization protocol step-by-step:
1. Power-on sequence
2. CMD0 (reset)
3. CMD8 (voltage check)
4. **ACMD41 loop** ← Most likely failure point
5. CMD58 (read OCR)
6. CMD17 (read sector)

## My Theory:

The CMD8 response `0x01 FF FF FF FF` instead of `0x01 00 00 01 AA` suggests:

**The card doesn't understand CMD8 or times out before sending the 4 response bytes.**

This could mean:
1. Card is SD v1.x (pre-2006) that doesn't support CMD8
2. Timing issue - card needs longer delays
3. Card enters wrong state after CMD0

Run **sd_deep_debug** - it will tell us if the card gets stuck at ACMD41 initialization (this is where most library failures happen).

If ACMD41 fails, the card won't complete initialization even though it responds to basic commands.

#define BAT_ADC 5  // From schematic

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== SD Card Power Check ===");

  // Check 3V3 rail via battery ADC
  analogReadResolution(12);
  int adcValue = analogRead(BAT_ADC);

  if (voltage < 3.5) {
    Serial.println("⚠ LOW BATTERY - Connect battery or use USB power");

  // Check 3V3 rail indirectly
  Serial.println("\nPower rail estimate:");
  Serial.println("USB only: ~3.3V");
  Serial.println("Battery: Depends on charge");
  Serial.println("\nSD cards need stable 3.0-3.6V");

  Serial.println("\n=== Recommendation ===");
  Serial.println("Try with battery connected:");
  Serial.println("  • Insert 3.7V LiPo battery");
  Serial.println("  • Keep USB plugged in");
  Serial.println("  • Battery + USB = more stable power");
}

void loop() {}

/*
 * SD v1.x initialization (legacy cards, pre-2006)
 * Your card might be old SD that doesn't support CMD8
 */

#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== SD v1.x Legacy Init ===");

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  delay(10);

  // Power-on clocks
  Serial.println("Sending init clocks...");
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // CMD0
  Serial.println("CMD0...");
  uint8_t r1 = sendCmd(0, 0, 0x95);
  Serial.printf("  R1: 0x%02X %s\n", r1, (r1 == 0x01) ? "✓" : "✗");

  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.println("CMD0 failed");
    return;
  }

  // Try CMD8 (will fail on v1.x cards)
  Serial.println("CMD8 (checking version)...");
  r1 = sendCmd(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  uint8_t r7[4];
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    r7[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  bool isV2 = (r1 == 0x01);
  Serial.printf("  Card type: SD v%s\n", isV2 ? "2.0+" : "1.x");

  // ACMD41 with longer timeout and different args
  Serial.println("\nACMD41 initialization:");
  int attempts = 0;
  bool success = false;

  while (attempts < 200) {  // More attempts
    // CMD55 first
    r1 = sendCmd(55, 0, 0xFF);
    if (r1 > 1) {
      Serial.printf("CMD55 error: 0x%02X\n", r1);
      break;
    }

    // ACMD41 - different arg for v1 vs v2
    uint32_t arg = isV2 ? 0x40000000 : 0x00000000;
    r1 = sendCmd(41, arg, 0xFF);

    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("  ✓ Initialized after %d attempts\n", attempts + 1);
      success = true;
      break;
    }

    if (attempts % 20 == 0) {
      Serial.printf("  Attempt %d: R1=0x%02X\n", attempts, r1);
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(20);  // Longer delay
  }

  if (!success) {
    Serial.printf("  ✗ Failed after %d attempts (R1=0x%02X)\n", attempts, r1);

    Serial.println("\n*** Card won't initialize ***");
    Serial.println("Possible causes:");
    Serial.println("  1. Insufficient power (try with battery)");
    Serial.println("  2. Incompatible card (some brands don't work)");
    Serial.println("  3. Card needs CMD1 (MMC) instead of ACMD41");
    Serial.println("  4. Card is damaged");

    // Try CMD1 (for MMC cards)
    Serial.println("\nTrying CMD1 (MMC mode)...");

    // Reset first
    sendCmd(0, 0, 0x95);
    delay(10);

    attempts = 0;
    while (attempts < 100) {
      r1 = sendCmd(1, 0, 0xFF);
      if (r1 == 0x00) {
        Serial.printf("  ✓ MMC card initialized after %d attempts\n", attempts + 1);
        success = true;
        break;
      }
      attempts++;
      delay(20);
    }

    if (!success) {
      Serial.println("  ✗ CMD1 also failed");
      Serial.println("\n=== Card is non-functional ===");
    }
    return;
  }

  // Read OCR
  Serial.println("\nCMD58 (READ_OCR)...");
  uint8_t ocr[5];
  ocr[0] = sendCmd(58, 0, 0xFF);

  }
  Serial.printf("  OCR: 0x%02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
                ocr[0], ocr[1], ocr[2], ocr[3], ocr[4]);

  bool isSDHC = (ocr[1] & 0x40);
  Serial.printf("  Type: %s\n", isSDHC ? "SDHC/SDXC" : "SDSC");

  Serial.println("\nCMD17 (read sector 0)...");

  Serial.printf("  R1: 0x%02X\n", r1);

    int timeout = 2000;
    while (timeout-- > 0) {
      token = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
      if (token == 0xFE) break;
      delayMicroseconds(100);

      Serial.println("  ✓ Data received");
      Serial.print("  First 16 bytes: ");
      for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
        Serial.printf("%02X ", SPI.transfer(0xFF));
      }
      for (int i = 16; i < 514; i++) {
        SPI.transfer(0xFF);
      }
      Serial.println("\n\n✓✓ CARD WORKS AT RAW LEVEL!");
    }
  }

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
}

void loop() {}

uint8_t sendCmd(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(50);  // Longer CS setup time

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  // Wait for response with longer timeout
  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
    delayMicroseconds(100);
  }

  return response;
}

/*
 * Working SD Card Implementation
 * Uses proven timing from sd_legacy_init
 */

#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"
#include "driver/sdspi_host.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Working SD Implementation ===");

  // Pre-init card with working timing
  if (!sdCardPreInit()) {
    Serial.println("Pre-init failed");
    return;
  }

  // Now try library with card already initialized
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  delay(100);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  // Try with custom config
  sdmmc_host_t host = SDSPI_HOST_DEFAULT();
  host.max_freq_khz = SDMMC_FREQ_PROBING; // 400kHz

  sdspi_device_config_t slot_config = SDSPI_DEVICE_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
  slot_config.gpio_cs = SD_CS;
  slot_config.host_id = host.slot;

  esp_vfs_fat_sdmmc_mount_config_t mount_config = {
    .format_if_mount_failed = false,
    .max_files = 5,
    .allocation_unit_size = 16 * 1024
  };

  sdmmc_card_t *card;
  esp_err_t ret = esp_vfs_fat_sdspi_mount("/sd", &host, &slot_config, &mount_config, &card);

  if (ret == ESP_OK) {
    Serial.println("✓✓ SD MOUNTED!");

    sdmmc_card_print_info(stdout, card);

    Serial.printf("Total: %lluMB\n", ((uint64_t)card->csd.capacity) * card->csd.sector_size / (1024 * 1024));

    testFileOperations();

    esp_vfs_fat_sdcard_unmount("/sd", card);
  } else {
    Serial.printf("✗ Mount failed: %s\n", esp_err_to_name(ret));

    // Fallback to simple SD.begin with longer timeout
    Serial.println("\nTrying simple method with delays...");

    SPI.end();
    delay(500);

    SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
    delay(500);

    if (SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI, 400000)) {
      Serial.println("✓✓ SD.begin() WORKED!");
      printCardInfo();
      testSDLibrary();
      SD.end();
    }
  }

  SPI.end();
}

void loop() {}

bool sdCardPreInit() {
  Serial.println("Pre-initializing card with working timing...");

  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  delay(100);

  // Send init clocks
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // CMD0
  uint8_t r1 = sendCmd(0, 0, 0x95);
  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.printf("CMD0 failed: 0x%02X\n", r1);
    return false;
  }

  // CMD8
  r1 = sendCmd(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // ACMD41 with longer delays
  int attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 200) {
    r1 = sendCmd(55, 0, 0xFF);
    if (r1 > 1) break;

    r1 = sendCmd(41, 0x40000000, 0xFF);
    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("Card ready after %d attempts\n", attempts + 1);

      digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
      SPI.transfer(0xFF);

      delay(100); // Important delay
      return true;
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(20); // Longer delay than library uses
  }

  Serial.printf("ACMD41 timeout\n");
  return false;
}

uint8_t sendCmd(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(50);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
    delayMicroseconds(100);
  }

  return response;
}

void printCardInfo() {
  uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();
  Serial.printf("Type: ");
  switch(cardType) {
    case CARD_MMC:  Serial.println("MMC"); break;
    case CARD_SD:   Serial.println("SDSC"); break;
    case CARD_SDHC: Serial.println("SDHC"); break;
    default:        Serial.println("UNKNOWN"); break;
  }

  uint64_t cardSize = SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024);
  Serial.printf("Size: %lluMB\n", cardSize);
  Serial.printf("Total: %lluMB\n", SD.totalBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
  Serial.printf("Used: %lluMB\n", SD.usedBytes() / (1024 * 1024));
}

void testSDLibrary() {
  Serial.println("\nTesting SD operations:");

  File root = SD.open("/");
  if (root) {
    Serial.println("Root directory:");
    File file = root.openNextFile();
    int count = 0;
    while (file && count < 10) {
      if (file.isDirectory()) {
        Serial.printf("  DIR: %s\n", file.name());
      } else {
        Serial.printf("  %s (%d bytes)\n", file.name(), file.size());
      }
      file = root.openNextFile();
      count++;
    }
    root.close();
  }

  File file = SD.open("/test_working.txt", FILE_WRITE);
  if (file) {
    file.println("SD card working!");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("Write: OK");

    file = SD.open("/test_working.txt");
    if (file) {
      Serial.print("Read: ");
      while(file.available()) {
        Serial.write(file.read());
      }
      file.close();
    }
    SD.remove("/test_working.txt");
  } else {
    Serial.println("Write: FAILED");
  }
}

void testFileOperations() {
  Serial.println("\nTesting file operations:");

  DIR *dir = opendir("/sd");
  if (dir) {
    Serial.println("Root directory:");
    struct dirent *entry;
    int count = 0;
    while ((entry = readdir(dir)) != NULL && count < 10) {
      Serial.printf("  %s\n", entry->d_name);
      count++;
    }
    closedir(dir);
  }

  FILE *f = fopen("/sd/test_esp.txt", "w");
  if (f) {
    fprintf(f, "ESP32-S3 SD test\n");
    fclose(f);
    Serial.println("Write: OK");

    f = fopen("/sd/test_esp.txt", "r");
    if (f) {
      char line[64];
      Serial.print("Read: ");
      while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
        Serial.print(line);
      }
      fclose(f);
    }
    remove("/sd/test_esp.txt");
  }
}

I've performed a web search for your query about ESP32-S3 SD card library SPI slow ACMD41 timeout issues. Here's what I found:

## ACMD41 Timeout Issues

The ACMD41 timeout problem occurs when SD cards continuously return busy (0x01 response) during initialization. This is a common initialization failure with ESP32 devices.

## Key Fixes and Alternatives

### 1. **SPI Initialization (ESP32-S3 Specific)**
On the ESP32-S3, there are no default SPI pins, so you need to manually begin the SPI interface to define the pins before initializing the SD card.

### 2. **Increase SPI Speed**
By default, the SD library sets the SPI speed at 4MHz, but 40MHz works much better on ESP32. You can set this with `SD.begin(cs_pin, spi, 40000000)`.

### 3. **SDK Version Matters**
PlatformIO-Arduino Framework V3.5.0 based on SDK V3.3.5 has SPI working 2 to 3 times faster than V2.0.0, suggesting that older SDK versions may perform better for SPI SD card operations.

### 4. **Use SD_MMC Instead**
If you want to use extended data lines, you should use the SD_MMC library instead of SPI, which can provide better performance.

### 5. **Buffering for Performance**
To increase write speed, allocate a large (16kB or 32kB) buffer and write using write(fileno(f), buffer, size) instead of fprintf.

The search results suggest the ACMD41 timeout is often related to improper SPI initialization on the S3, slow default speeds, or SDK version incompatibilities rather than a fundamental hardware issue.

## SdFat Library Performance on ESP32

The SdFat library appears to be faster than the implementation of FATFs in esp-idf libraries, according to discussions in the ESP32 forum.

### Significant Performance Advantage

SdFat library appears to be 85 time faster than Espressif SD library in testing with 100 files at 20 MHz. Specifically:
- Espressif SD library: 66,228 ms (1'06")
- SdFat library: 771 ms

### About the SdFat Library

SdFat Version 2 supports FAT16/FAT32 and exFAT SD cards and offers several advanced features. The library is developed by Bill Greiman and is available on his GitHub repository (greiman/SdFat).

If the SD card is the only SPI device, use dedicated SPI mode. This can greatly improve performance.

### ESP32 Compatibility

There's a forked version specifically optimized for ESP32 (SdFat-ESP32) that includes adjustments to SdFat_config.h to suit ESP32 target with settings for block device support and SPI configuration.

The library supports ESP32 architecture and provides substantially better performance than the standard Arduino SD.h library for file operations, particularly when dealing with multiple files or large datasets.

Based on the search results, here are the main solutions for ESP32 SD card ACMD41 initialization failures in 2024:

## Common Solutions for ACMD41 Initialization Failures

### 1. **Add a Delay Before Mounting**
A delay of a few milliseconds between spi_bus_initialize and sdspi_mount can help the SD card consistently work at every boot, allowing initialization to succeed close to 100% of the time.(no content)This delay allows time for voltage to stabilize on the device or SD card breakout board.

### 2. **Check Pull-up Resistors**
SD card pins need pull-up resistors to work correctly.(no content)Adding pullup resistors to SD card breakout boards that don't have them can help resolve initialization issues.

### 3. **Handle GPIO12 Conflict**
GPIO12 acts as both an SD card pin and a bootstrapping pin that controls flash voltage at reset (1.8V if high, 3.3V if low), requiring the pin to be pulled high for SD card operation but low for 3.3V flash modules.(no content)To resolve this conflict, use espefuse.py tool to program the flash voltage efuse of the chip for 3.3V.

### 4. **Adjust Initialization Timing**
Some SD cards are picky about the number of 'dummy' SPI clocks required before the first SPI command is issued.(no content)Playing around with pre-initialization signals and the timing/delay before/between initialization commands can get cards to work that originally wouldn't.

### 5. **Reduce SPI Frequency**
Lowering the frequency to 400kHz during initialization may help, though the Arduino framework starts with 400kHz and then increases to 4000kHz for data transfer.

### 6. **Card Compatibility**
Different SD cards are flaky or picky about their initialization sequence to varying degrees, but if a card is successfully initialized for SPI interface, the rest typically works too.

The most commonly reported successful fix in 2024 discussions is adding a delay before the mount operation to allow voltage stabilization.

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  // Configure SdFat with slower speed and dedicated SPI
  SdSpiConfig config(SD_CS, DEDICATED_SPI, SD_SCK_MHZ(1), &SPI);

  Serial.println("Initializing SD card...");

  if (!sd.begin(config)) {
    Serial.println("Trying even slower (400kHz)...");
    SdSpiConfig slowConfig(SD_CS, DEDICATED_SPI, SD_SCK_HZ(400000), &SPI);

    if (!sd.begin(slowConfig)) {
      if (sd.card()->errorCode()) {
        Serial.printf("SD errorCode: 0x%X, 0x%X\n",
          (int)sd.card()->errorCode(),
          (int)sd.card()->errorData());
      }
      Serial.println("✗ SD init failed");
      return;
    }
  }

  Serial.println("✓ SD Initialized!");

  // Print card info
  printCardInfo();

  // Test all operations
  testAllOperations();
}

void loop() {}

void printCardInfo() {
  Serial.println("\n--- Card Info ---");

  uint32_t cardSectorCount = sd.card()->sectorCount();
  Serial.printf("Type: %s\n",
    sd.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SDHC ? "SDHC" :
    sd.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SD2 ? "SD2" : "SD1");

  Serial.printf("Size: %lu MB\n", (cardSectorCount / 2048));

  uint32_t volumesize = sd.vol()->clusterCount() * sd.vol()->blocksPerCluster() / 2048;
  Serial.printf("Volume: %lu MB\n", volumesize);

  Serial.printf("Free: %lu MB\n",
    (sd.vol()->freeClusterCount() * sd.vol()->blocksPerCluster()) / 2048);
}

void testAllOperations() {
  Serial.println("\n=== Testing All File Operations ===");

  // 1. LIST ROOT
  Serial.println("\n1. List root directory:");
  if (!dir.open("/")) {
    Serial.println("  Failed to open root");
    return;
  }

  int count = 0;
  while (file.openNext(&dir, O_RDONLY)) {
    char name[64];
    file.getName(name, sizeof(name));

    if (file.isDir()) {
      Serial.printf("  DIR:  %s\n", name);
    } else {
      Serial.printf("  FILE: %-20s %10lu bytes\n", name, (unsigned long)file.fileSize());
    }

    file.close();
    if (++count > 10) break;
  }
  dir.close();

  // 2. WRITE FILE
  Serial.println("\n2. Write file:");
  if (file.open("/test_sdfat.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC)) {
    file.println("SdFat library test");
    file.println("All operations working!");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("  ✓ Write OK");
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Write failed");
  }

  // 3. READ FILE
  Serial.println("\n3. Read file:");
  if (file.open("/test_sdfat.txt", O_RDONLY)) {
    Serial.println("  Content:");
    while (file.available()) {
      Serial.write(file.read());
    }
    file.close();
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Read failed");
  }

  // 4. APPEND TO FILE
  Serial.println("\n4. Append to file:");
  if (file.open("/test_sdfat.txt", O_WRONLY | O_APPEND)) {
    file.println("Appended line");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("  ✓ Append OK");
  }

  // 5. RENAME FILE
  Serial.println("\n5. Rename file:");
  if (sd.rename("/test_sdfat.txt", "/renamed.txt")) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ Renamed test_sdfat.txt -> renamed.txt");
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Rename failed");
  }

  // 6. CREATE DIRECTORY
  Serial.println("\n6. Create directory:");
  if (sd.mkdir("/testdir")) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ Created /testdir");
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ mkdir failed (may already exist)");
  }

  // 7. WRITE IN SUBDIRECTORY
  Serial.println("\n7. Write in subdirectory:");
  if (file.open("/testdir/subfile.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC)) {
    file.println("File in subdirectory");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("  ✓ Created /testdir/subfile.txt");
  }

  // 8. FILE SIZE
  Serial.println("\n8. Get file size:");
  if (file.open("/renamed.txt", O_RDONLY)) {
    Serial.printf("  Size: %lu bytes\n", (unsigned long)file.fileSize());
    file.close();
  }

  // 9. FILE EXISTS
  Serial.println("\n9. Check if file exists:");
  Serial.printf("  /renamed.txt: %s\n", sd.exists("/renamed.txt") ? "EXISTS" : "NOT FOUND");
  Serial.printf("  /missing.txt: %s\n", sd.exists("/missing.txt") ? "EXISTS" : "NOT FOUND");

  // 10. DELETE FILE
  Serial.println("\n10. Delete files:");
  if (sd.remove("/renamed.txt")) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ Deleted /renamed.txt");
  }

  // 11. REMOVE DIRECTORY (must be empty)
  Serial.println("\n11. Remove directory:");
  if (sd.remove("/testdir/subfile.txt") && sd.rmdir("/testdir")) {
    Serial.println("  ✓ Removed /testdir");
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ rmdir failed");
  }

  // 12. LARGE FILE WRITE (performance test)
  Serial.println("\n12. Large file write (1MB):");
  uint32_t startTime = millis();
  if (file.open("/large.bin", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC)) {
    uint8_t buf[512];
    memset(buf, 0xAA, sizeof(buf));

    for (int i = 0; i < 2048; i++) {  // 2048 * 512 = 1MB
      file.write(buf, sizeof(buf));
    }
    file.close();

    uint32_t elapsed = millis() - startTime;
    Serial.printf("  ✓ Wrote 1MB in %lu ms (%.2f KB/s)\n",
      elapsed, 1024.0 / (elapsed / 1000.0));

    sd.remove("/large.bin");
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Large write failed");
  }

  Serial.println("\n✓✓✓ ALL OPERATIONS COMPLETE ✓✓✓");
  Serial.println("\nSdFat library provides:");
  Serial.println("  • read/write/append files");
  Serial.println("  • create/delete directories");
  Serial.println("  • rename/move files");
  Serial.println("  • check existence");
  Serial.println("  • list directories");
  Serial.println("  • exFAT support (>32GB cards)");
}

SdFat library is better because:
- More flexible timeout handling
- Better ESP32 support
- 85x faster
- Complete file operations

The sketch should compile and work now with the API fix!

/*
 * SdFat with manual pre-init using proven timing
 */

#include "SPI.h"
#include "SdFat.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

SdFat sd;
FsFile file;
FsFile dir;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== SdFat with Pre-Init ===");

  // Manual pre-init with working timing
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  Serial.println("Pre-initializing card...");

  delay(100);

  // Send dummy clocks
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // CMD0
  uint8_t r1 = sendCmd(0, 0, 0x95);
  Serial.printf("CMD0: 0x%02X %s\n", r1, (r1 == 0x01) ? "OK" : "FAIL");

  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.println("CMD0 failed, aborting");
    return;
  }

  // CMD8
  r1 = sendCmd(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // ACMD41 with long delays
  Serial.println("ACMD41 loop (this may take 10-20 seconds)...");
  int attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 200) {
    r1 = sendCmd(55, 0, 0xFF);
    if (r1 > 1) break;

    r1 = sendCmd(41, 0x40000000, 0xFF);
    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("Ready after %d attempts\n", attempts + 1);
      digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
      SPI.transfer(0xFF);
      break;
    }

    if (attempts % 20 == 0) {
      Serial.printf("  Attempt %d...\n", attempts);
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(20); // Long delay
  }

  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    Serial.printf("ACMD41 timeout (R1=0x%02X)\n", r1);
    return;
  }

  delay(100);

  // Now try SdFat
  Serial.println("\nInitializing SdFat library...");

  SdSpiConfig config(SD_CS, DEDICATED_SPI, SD_SCK_MHZ(10), &SPI);

  if (!sd.begin(config)) {
    Serial.println("SdFat init failed (but card is pre-initialized)");
    Serial.println("Trying lower speed...");

    SdSpiConfig slowConfig(SD_CS, DEDICATED_SPI, SD_SCK_MHZ(1), &SPI);
    if (!sd.begin(slowConfig)) {
      Serial.println("Still failed - card initialized but SdFat can't use it");
      return;
    }
  }

  Serial.println("✓✓ SdFat WORKING!");

  printCardInfo();
  testOperations();
}

void loop() {}

uint8_t sendCmd(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(50);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
    delayMicroseconds(100);
  }

  return response;
}

void printCardInfo() {
  Serial.println("\n--- Card Info ---");

  uint32_t cardSectorCount = sd.card()->sectorCount();
  Serial.printf("Type: %s\n",
    sd.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SDHC ? "SDHC" :
    sd.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SD2 ? "SD2" : "SD1");

  Serial.printf("Size: %lu MB\n", (cardSectorCount / 2048));

  uint32_t volumesize = sd.vol()->clusterCount() * sd.vol()->sectorsPerCluster() / 2048;
  Serial.printf("Volume: %lu MB\n", volumesize);

  Serial.printf("Free: %lu MB\n",
    (sd.vol()->freeClusterCount() * sd.vol()->sectorsPerCluster()) / 2048);
}

void testOperations() {
  Serial.println("\n=== File Operations Test ===");

  // List root
  Serial.println("\nRoot directory:");
  if (dir.open("/")) {
    int count = 0;
    while (file.openNext(&dir, O_RDONLY) && count < 10) {
      char name[64];
      file.getName(name, sizeof(name));
      Serial.printf("  %s (%lu bytes)\n", name, (unsigned long)file.fileSize());
      file.close();
      count++;
    }
    dir.close();
  }

  // Write test
  Serial.println("\nWrite test:");
  if (file.open("/sdfat_test.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC)) {
    file.println("SdFat working!");
    file.println("All operations available");
    file.close();
    Serial.println("  ✓ Write OK");
  }

  // Read test
  Serial.println("\nRead test:");
  if (file.open("/sdfat_test.txt", O_RDONLY)) {
    while (file.available()) {
      Serial.write(file.read());
    }
    file.close();
  }

  // Cleanup
  sd.remove("/sdfat_test.txt");

  Serial.println("\n✓✓✓ ALL TESTS PASSED ✓✓✓");
  Serial.println("\nYour SD card works perfectly!");
  Serial.println("Use SdFat for all future projects.");
}

void loop() {}

void testArduinoSD(uint32_t freq) {
  Serial.printf("\nTrying SD.h @ %lu Hz (%.1f MHz)...\n", freq, freq/1000000.0);

  SPI.end();
  delay(100);
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  unsigned long startTime = millis();
  bool success = SD.begin(SD_CS, SPI, freq);
  unsigned long elapsed = millis() - startTime;

  Serial.printf("  Init time: %lu ms\n", elapsed);

  if (success) {
    Serial.println("  ✓✓ MOUNTED!");

    uint8_t cardType = SD.cardType();
    if (cardType != CARD_NONE) {
      Serial.printf("  Type: ");
      switch(cardType) {
        case CARD_MMC:  Serial.println("MMC"); break;
        case CARD_SD:   Serial.println("SDSC"); break;
        case CARD_SDHC: Serial.println("SDHC"); break;
        default:        Serial.println("UNKNOWN"); break;
      }

      uint64_t cardSize = SD.cardSize() / (1024 * 1024);
      Serial.printf("  Size: %llu MB\n", cardSize);
      Serial.printf("  Used: %llu MB\n", SD.usedBytes() / (1024 * 1024));

      // List files
      Serial.println("  Files (max 10):");
      File root = SD.open("/");
      if (root) {
        int count = 0;
        File file = root.openNextFile();
        while (file && count < 10) {
          if (!file.isDirectory()) {
            Serial.printf("    %s (%d bytes)\n", file.name(), file.size());
          }
          file = root.openNextFile();
          count++;
        }
        root.close();
      }

      Serial.println("\n  *** SD.h WORKS - Use this! ***");
    }

    SD.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Failed");
  }

  if (elapsed > 5000) {
    Serial.println("  (took too long - timeout likely)");
  }
}

void testSdFat(uint32_t freq) {
  Serial.printf("\nTrying SdFat @ %lu Hz (%.1f MHz)...\n", freq, freq/1000000.0);

  SPI.end();
  delay(100);
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);

  SdSpiConfig config(SD_CS, DEDICATED_SPI, freq, &SPI);

  unsigned long startTime = millis();
  bool success = sdfat.begin(config);
  unsigned long elapsed = millis() - startTime;

  Serial.printf("  Init time: %lu ms\n", elapsed);

  if (success) {
    Serial.println("  ✓✓ MOUNTED!");

    Serial.printf("  Type: %s\n",
      sdfat.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SDHC ? "SDHC" :
      sdfat.card()->type() == SD_CARD_TYPE_SD2 ? "SD2" : "SD1");

    uint32_t cardSectorCount = sdfat.card()->sectorCount();
    Serial.printf("  Size: %lu MB\n", (cardSectorCount / 2048));

    uint32_t freeSpace = (sdfat.vol()->freeClusterCount() * sdfat.vol()->sectorsPerCluster()) / 2048;
    Serial.printf("  Free: %lu MB\n", freeSpace);

    // List files
    Serial.println("  Files (max 10):");
    FsFile root, file;
    if (root.open("/")) {
      int count = 0;
      while (file.openNext(&root, O_RDONLY) && count < 10) {
        if (!file.isDir()) {
          char name[64];
          file.getName(name, sizeof(name));
          Serial.printf("    %s (%lu bytes)\n", name, (unsigned long)file.fileSize());
        }
        file.close();
        count++;
      }
      root.close();
    }

    Serial.println("\n  *** SdFat WORKS - Use this! ***");

    sdfat.end();
  } else {
    Serial.println("  ✗ Failed");

    if (sdfat.card()->errorCode()) {
      Serial.printf("  Error: 0x%X / 0x%X\n",
        sdfat.card()->errorCode(),
        sdfat.card()->errorData());
    }
  }

  if (elapsed > 5000) {
    Serial.println("  (took too long - timeout likely)");
  }
}

/*
 * Direct SD Card Access - No Library Dependencies
 * Uses raw protocol that we know works
 * Provides simple read/write functions
 */

#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

bool sdInitialized = false;
bool isSDHC = false;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== Raw SD Card Access ===");

  if (!sdInit()) {
    Serial.println("✗ SD init failed");
    return;
  }

  Serial.println("✓ SD initialized!");

  // Test: Read sector 0 (MBR/Boot sector)
  Serial.println("\n--- Reading Sector 0 (MBR) ---");
  uint8_t buffer[512];

  if (sdReadSector(0, buffer)) {
    Serial.println("✓ Sector 0 read successfully");

    // Show first 64 bytes
    Serial.println("First 64 bytes:");
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
      Serial.printf("%02X ", buffer[i]);
      if ((i + 1) % 16 == 0) Serial.println();
    }

    // Check MBR signature
    if (buffer[510] == 0x55 && buffer[511] == 0xAA) {
      Serial.println("\n✓ Valid MBR signature");

      // Parse partition table
      Serial.println("\nPartition Table:");
      for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        uint8_t *entry = &buffer[446 + (i * 16)];
        uint8_t type = entry[4];

        if (type != 0) {
          uint32_t lbaStart = *((uint32_t*)&entry[8]);
          uint32_t sectors = *((uint32_t*)&entry[12]);

          Serial.printf("  Partition %d: Type=0x%02X, Start=%lu, Size=%lu MB\n",
            i, type, lbaStart, (sectors / 2048));

          if (type == 0x0B || type == 0x0C) {
            Serial.println("    ^ FAT32 partition");
          }
        }
      }
    }
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ Failed to read sector 0");
  }

  // Test: Write and read back a sector (sector 1000 is usually safe)
  Serial.println("\n--- Write/Read Test (Sector 1000) ---");

  uint8_t writeData[512];
  for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
    writeData[i] = i & 0xFF;
  }

  Serial.println("Writing test pattern...");
  if (sdWriteSector(1000, writeData)) {
    Serial.println("✓ Write successful");

    uint8_t readData[512];
    Serial.println("Reading back...");

    if (sdReadSector(1000, readData)) {
      Serial.println("✓ Read successful");

      // Verify
      bool match = true;
      for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
        if (readData[i] != writeData[i]) {
          match = false;
          break;
        }
      }

      if (match) {
        Serial.println("✓✓ DATA VERIFIED - Read/Write Working!");
      } else {
        Serial.println("✗ Data mismatch");
      }
    }
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ Write failed");
  }

  Serial.println("\n=== Raw SD Access Working ===");
  Serial.println("Your card works perfectly at hardware level!");
  Serial.println("\nNext step: Build FAT32 parser or use");
  Serial.println("external FAT library (FatFs, elm-chan)");
}

void loop() {}

bool sdInit() {
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  delay(100);

  // Dummy clocks
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // CMD0
  Serial.print("CMD0... ");
  uint8_t r1 = sdCommand(0, 0, 0x95);
  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.printf("FAIL (0x%02X)\n", r1);
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // CMD8
  Serial.print("CMD8... ");
  r1 = sdCommand(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  uint32_t r7 = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    r7 = (r7 << 8) | SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  bool isV2 = (r1 == 0x01);
  Serial.printf("%s\n", isV2 ? "SD v2.0+" : "SD v1.x");

  // ACMD41
  Serial.print("ACMD41... ");
  int attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 200) {
    sdCommand(55, 0, 0xFF);
    r1 = sdCommand(41, isV2 ? 0x40000000 : 0, 0xFF);

    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("Ready (%d attempts)\n", attempts + 1);
      break;
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(20);
  }

  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    Serial.printf("TIMEOUT (0x%02X)\n", r1);
    return false;
  }

  // CMD58
  Serial.print("CMD58... ");
  uint8_t ocr[5];
  ocr[0] = sdCommand(58, 0, 0xFF);
  for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
    ocr[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  isSDHC = (ocr[1] & 0x40);
  Serial.printf("%s\n", isSDHC ? "SDHC/SDXC" : "SDSC");

  // Switch to faster speed
  SPI.setFrequency(10000000);

  // CMD16 (set block size for SDSC)
  if (!isSDHC) {
    Serial.print("CMD16... ");
    r1 = sdCommand(16, 512, 0xFF);
    Serial.println(r1 == 0 ? "OK" : "FAIL");
  }

  sdInitialized = true;
  return true;
}

uint8_t sdCommand(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(50);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
    delayMicroseconds(100);
  }

  return response;
}

bool sdReadSector(uint32_t sector, uint8_t *buffer) {
  if (!sdInitialized) return false;

  uint32_t address = isSDHC ? sector : sector * 512;

  uint8_t r1 = sdCommand(17, address, 0xFF);
  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    return false;
  }

  // Wait for data token
  uint8_t token;
  int timeout = 10000;
  while (timeout-- > 0) {
    token = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (token == 0xFE) break;
  }

  if (token != 0xFE) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    return false;
  }

  // Read 512 bytes
  for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
    buffer[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // Read CRC (ignore)
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  return true;
}

bool sdWriteSector(uint32_t sector, const uint8_t *buffer) {
  if (!sdInitialized) return false;

  uint32_t address = isSDHC ? sector : sector * 512;

  uint8_t r1 = sdCommand(24, address, 0xFF);
  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    return false;
  }

  // Send data token
  SPI.transfer(0xFE);

  // Write 512 bytes
  for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(buffer[i]);
  }

  // Dummy CRC
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  // Check response
  uint8_t response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  if ((response & 0x1F) != 0x05) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    return false;
  }

  // Wait for write to complete
  int timeout = 10000;
  while (timeout-- > 0) {
    if (SPI.transfer(0xFF) != 0x00) break;
  }

  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  return true;
}

## FatFs Library for ESP32 with Arduino

### Overview
FatFs is a lightweight software library for microcontrollers and embedded systems that implements FAT/exFAT file system support, written on pure ANSI C and platform-independent. The library was originally created by elm-chan and IDF uses the FatFs library to work with FAT file systems.

### Installation Methods

**1. Arduino Core Integration**
At the time FAT file system support was added to the Arduino core, the recommendation was to pull the latest code from the GitHub repository of the Arduino core to get these changes.

**2. ESP32 FatFS Plugin (Recommended)**
There's an Arduino plugin which packs sketch data folder into FatFS filesystem image and uploads the image to ESP32 flash memory. The plugin is available at the lorol/arduino-esp32fatfs-plugin repository.

### Basic Setup Steps

**Partition Configuration**
Without changing the default partition definition, mounting would fail because there is no partition for the FAT file system, so you need to edit the default schema to change the partition of the SPIFFS file system to a partition for a FAT file system.

**Code Usage**
You need to import the "FFat.h" library to have access to all the functionalities needed to interact with the file system. FFat.begin(formatIfNeeded = false) mounts FFat file system and must be called before any other FS APIs are used, returning true if file system was mounted successfully.

**Memory Considerations**
The FFAT module uses 8KB plus 4KB per concurrent file that can be opened, and by default allows 10 files to be opened, which means it uses 48KB.

You can find the official FatFs documentation and source at elm-chan's website (http://elm-chan.org/fsw/ff/00index_e.html).

/*
 * FatFs with Custom SD Driver
 * Uses your working SD init + FatFs for file operations
 *
 * Install: Library Manager -> "FatFs" by ChaN
 * Or download from: http://elm-chan.org/fsw/ff/00index_e.html
 */

#include "SPI.h"

#define SD_CS   41
#define SD_MOSI 38
#define SD_MISO 40
#define SD_SCK  39

// Simple SD driver state
bool sdReady = false;
bool isSDHC = false;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(2000);

  Serial.println("\n=== SD Card with FatFs ===");

  // Initialize SD card
  if (!initSD()) {
    Serial.println("✗ SD init failed");
    return;
  }

  Serial.println("✓ SD card ready!");

  // For now, just demonstrate raw sector access works
  // In next step, we'll integrate FatFs

  testRawAccess();
}

void loop() {}

bool initSD() {
  pinMode(SD_CS, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);

  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  SPI.setFrequency(400000);

  // Add power-up delay
  delay(200);

  // Send 80 clocks with CS high (card power-up)
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }
  delay(10);

  // CMD0 - GO_IDLE_STATE
  Serial.print("CMD0... ");
  uint8_t r1 = sendCommand(0, 0, 0x95);
  if (r1 != 0x01) {
    Serial.printf("FAIL (0x%02X)\n", r1);
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");
  delay(10);

  // CMD8 - SEND_IF_COND
  Serial.print("CMD8... ");
  r1 = sendCommand(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
  uint8_t r7[4];
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    r7[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  bool isV2 = (r1 == 0x01);
  Serial.println(isV2 ? "v2.0+" : "v1.x");
  delay(10);

  // ACMD41 - SD_SEND_OP_COND
  Serial.print("ACMD41... ");
  int attempts = 0;

  while (attempts < 200) {
    // CMD55 - APP_CMD
    r1 = sendCommand(55, 0, 0xFF);
    if (r1 > 1) {
      Serial.printf("CMD55 error (0x%02X)\n", r1);
      return false;
    }

    // ACMD41
    r1 = sendCommand(41, isV2 ? 0x40000000 : 0, 0xFF);

    if (r1 == 0x00) {
      Serial.printf("Ready (%d)\n", attempts + 1);
      break;
    }

    attempts++;
    delay(20);  // Critical delay
  }

  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    Serial.printf("TIMEOUT (0x%02X)\n", r1);
    return false;
  }

  delay(10);

  // CMD58 - READ_OCR
  Serial.print("CMD58... ");
  uint8_t ocr[5];
  ocr[0] = sendCommand(58, 0, 0xFF);
  for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
    ocr[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  isSDHC = (ocr[1] & 0x40);
  Serial.println(isSDHC ? "SDHC" : "SDSC");

  // Speed up to 10MHz
  SPI.setFrequency(10000000);

  // CMD16 - SET_BLOCKLEN (for SDSC only)
  if (!isSDHC) {
    Serial.print("CMD16... ");
    r1 = sendCommand(16, 512, 0xFF);
    Serial.println(r1 == 0 ? "OK" : "FAIL");
  }

  sdReady = true;
  return true;
}

uint8_t sendCommand(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc) {
  // Pulse CS high then low
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  delayMicroseconds(100);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(100);

  // Send command
  SPI.transfer(0x40 | cmd);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((arg >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(arg & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(crc);

  // Wait for response
  uint8_t response;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    response = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(response & 0x80)) break;
    delayMicroseconds(100);
  }

  // End command
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  return response;
}

void testRawAccess() {
  Serial.println("\n--- Raw Sector Test ---");

  uint8_t buffer[512];

  if (readSector(0, buffer)) {
    Serial.println("✓ Sector 0 read OK");

    // Show MBR signature
    Serial.printf("MBR sig: 0x%02X%02X ", buffer[511], buffer[510]);
    if (buffer[510] == 0x55 && buffer[511] == 0xAA) {
      Serial.println("✓");
    } else {
      Serial.println("✗");
    }

    // Show first partition entry
    uint8_t *p = &buffer[446];
    uint8_t type = p[4];
    if (type != 0) {
      uint32_t start = *((uint32_t*)&p[8]);
      Serial.printf("Partition 0: Type=0x%02X, Start=%lu\n", type, start);
    }
  } else {
    Serial.println("✗ Read failed");
  }

  Serial.println("\n✓✓ SD card working at sector level!");
  Serial.println("\nNext: Integrate FatFs or use elm-chan library");
}

bool readSector(uint32_t sector, uint8_t *buffer) {
  if (!sdReady) return false;

  uint32_t addr = isSDHC ? sector : (sector * 512);

  // CMD17 - READ_SINGLE_BLOCK
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  delayMicroseconds(100);
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(100);

  SPI.transfer(0x40 | 17);
  SPI.transfer((addr >> 24) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((addr >> 16) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer((addr >> 8) & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(addr & 0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  // Wait for R1
  uint8_t r1;
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    r1 = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (!(r1 & 0x80)) break;
  }

  if (r1 != 0x00) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    return false;
  }

  // Wait for data token
  uint8_t token;
  int timeout = 100000;
  while (timeout-- > 0) {
    token = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    if (token == 0xFE) break;
  }

  if (token != 0xFE) {
    digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
    SPI.transfer(0xFF);
    return false;
  }

  // Read data
  for (int i = 0; i < 512; i++) {
    buffer[i] = SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  }

  // Read CRC (discard)
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  // End transfer
  digitalWrite(SD_CS, HIGH);
  SPI.transfer(0xFF);

  return true;
}
